original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).
notes: Catalog statement recovered 2026-09-30. Round 3: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true, missing_theorems=[jsp_000140_main]. Round 3 added lean/JSPProblem/Construction.lean (new file, zero sorry): the classical sum/round-robin colouring c(s(a,b)) = a+b mod m of K_n with m colours (n <= m) -- admissible_sumColMod: for ODD m every K_4 spans at least five colours; its two structural ingredients are properness (sumColMod_adj_ne) and the fact that at most one pair of opposite edges of a K_4 shares a colour (sumColMod_one_collision, because two collisions would force 2(a-d)=0 in ZMod m and 2 is invertible for odd m, two_mul_inj). Consequences: EG_le_sumCol (f(n,4,5) <= n for odd n), EG_le_succ (f(n,4,5) <= n+1 for all n) and hence f(n,4,5) = Theta(n). Main.lean gained the first genuine two-sided statement about the headline constant: fiveSixthShape |f(n,4,5) - 5n/6| <= n/6 + 1 for n >= 4 (i.e. f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + O(n)), plus fiveSixth_ge_one (the headline estimate for every eps >= 1), fiveSixthUpper_at_third / admissibleUpper_at_third (the upper half for eps >= 1/3), fiveSixthUpper_odd_at_sixth / fiveSixthUpper_odd_ge (the upper half for odd n already at eps = 1/6) and admissibleLower_at_third (the lower half in colouring form for eps >= 1/3). Still missing for jsp_000140_main: the BCDP22 sharpening 3/4 -> 5/6 for the lower half (0 < eps < 1/8) and the BCDP22 construction for the upper half (0 < eps < 1/3).
